title: Undo and Redo on a video answer at once
goal: On a video, Command Z and Shift Command Z hold the app for about a fifth of a second after a cut, a ripple delete or a clip drop, which an editor feels on every undo while cutting. Bring Undo and Redo on the timeline under the 50 ms the video goals ask for.
notes:
Reproduced 2026-10-07 by the manager pass, probe from HEAD 8cfad4ee, timedWithoutMarkers, two runs of /tmp/mgr-walks/undo-cost.json (openSampleTalk, Add Track > Captions, Command K at a quarter, undo, Command K twice, Delete, undo, redo, drop b-roll at 12.9 s, undo, redo):
  undo of a cut:            longest 165.8 / 168.3 ms, from ~236 ms after the press
  undo of a ripple delete:  221.5 / 217.2 ms, from ~249 ms
  redo of it:               207.1 / 207.8 ms, from ~260 ms
  undo of a clip drop:      200.0 / 205.9 ms, from ~240 ms
  redo of it:               202.6 / 207.7 ms
For scale, the presses themselves: Command K 73-85 ms, Delete 23-30 ms. The hold starts about a quarter second AFTER the undo, so it is deferred work, not the undo itself. Start by finding what runs ~240 ms after History undo/redo on a video (a debounced job: thumbnails, waveform, captions re-layout, autosave, panel sections built a frame at a time?).
Same shape in the 12:36 an-editing-session-walk (probe in front): after clicking Animate a property, longest 288 ms from 408 ms in; after picking Position, 311 ms from 485 ms in. If one deferred job explains both, say so in clicking-a-cut-keying-a-value-and-undoing-it-ans's log (that task, blocked on a card, owns the key and its undo).
Undo of a KEY is that task's, not this one's. The digest's process note applies: if the cause sits outside the code this task touches, stop and say so rather than filing the next speed task.
acceptance: A timed walk (new, or an extension of an existing perf walk) undoes and redoes a cut, a ripple delete and a clip drop on the talk sample with captions, and each holds the main thread under 50 ms in nine of ten presses over three runs, none over 100 ms
The picture, the timeline and the panel after each Undo and Redo are the same as today (the walk checks the clip pieces and the captions' last line)
If the cost turns out to be something a person would see change (a lane or the picture resizing), stop, open a decision card with the measurements, and block, rather than filing another speed task
Audit written under queue/audits/ with before and after numbers; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Reproduced first (HEAD 4e93f5dc, the manager's walk): waits after undo/redo read 166-222ms from ~250ms in. Not the app: (1) same walk with videoPause in place of every undo/redo, the waits read under 2ms; (2) with the markers left up throughout, no deferred hold at all, undo/redo 45-64ms at 0ms in; (3) delaying the harness's marker re-hang by 1s moved the hold to 1341-1359ms in. The hold was the walk putting its ~800 marker views back up after a document change.

Fixed in the harness (a226b321): putTheMarkersBackUp lets the app go quiet first (<=0.5s, on the meter), then takes the re-hang off the meter (mark/forget) and names it on the wait line. New Scripts/playtest/undo-redo-cost-walk.json: undo+redo of a cut, a ripple delete and a b-roll drop, 10 presses, waits fail at 100ms, pieces + every caption line checked after each press. 3 runs green: presses 46-77ms (3 of 30 under 50), no deferred hold, none over 100.

Where the ~55ms press goes (Time Profiler, xctrace, 24 undo/redo): app code ~10ms spread thin (InspectorPanel/TimelineDock/ClipPiecesBar bodies, Dropdown.updateNSView ~1ms); ~20% SwiftUI accessibility upkeep (AccessibilityViewGraph.update/needsUpdate, focus responder walk); the rest SwiftUI graph update + layout of the editor, the same cost every edit pays (Command K 60-85ms). Not undo-specific, so per the process note it is not a new speed task: folded into clicking-a-cut-keying-a-value-and-undoing-it-ans (acceptance item added, walk named).

left rough: opening the Export sheet on a video holds 363ms in its own pass (an-editing-session-walk step 82, exportDialogAsVideo). One-off per export and the sheet animates in; not filed, recorded here.

The hold this was filed on was the walk harness, not the app: the 166-222ms after every Undo/Redo was the walk's markers going back up (delaying the re-hang 1s moved the hold 1s; no-op actions read <2ms). Fixed in the harness and guarded by the new undo-redo-cost-walk (a226b321): no deferred hold after any press, none over 100ms, pieces and caption lines unchanged, 3 runs green, plus an-editing-session, clip-click-cost, keyframe-anything and animate-pick-cost green, 11765 tests. What is left, presses of 46-77ms, is the cost every edit on a video pays (Command K costs more), not undo's, so per the process note it is folded into clicking-a-cut-keying-a-value-and-undoing-it-ans as an acceptance item rather than filed again. No audit: nothing a person sees changed.
